title: If only someone told me this before my 1st startup: 20 hard-won founder rules
summary: John Rush lists 20 lessons from years of failed startups: validate first, bootstrap, go B2B and global, hire only doers, do SEO and daily posting early, and skip corporates, hype and conferences. Each rule is backed by a personal cost, like 5 wasted years or 14 years ignoring SEO.

principles.text: Validate the idea before building; building unwanted products wastes years.
principles.quote: Validate idea first. I wasted at least 5 years building stuff nobody needed.

principles.text: Chase users, not investors; investors follow traction.
principles.quote: Don't chaise investors, chase users, and then investors will be chasing you.

principles.text: Presell features: chat with 10-20 users daily and build only what resonates.
principles.quote: Sell features, before building them. Ask existing users if they want this feature.

principles.text: Keep the landing page simple; most visitors arrive with intent from content or recommendations.
principles.quote: 90% of the users will end up on your site coming from a blog article, social media post, a recommendation. Which means they have the intent. No need to "convert" them again.

principles.text: Start SEO as early as possible; ignoring it was a huge regret.
principles.quote: Do SEO from day 2. As early as you can. I ignored this for 14 years. It's my biggest regret.

principles.text: Go global from day 1 because the upside is far bigger if it works.
principles.quote: If the product and marketing are good, it will work on the global market too, if it's bad, it won't work on the local market too.
